transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-25 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Emma Torres (CISO, Silverpike), Raj Patel (Head of Platform), Olivia Chen (Legal), Leo Martinez (DevOps)

Summary:
Redwood AE+SE ran a security posture intake to understand Silverpike's compliance requirements and deployment preferences. Main topics: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and RBAC integration, KMS/HSM key control, audit logs and retention, data residency and retention policies, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, pilot scope and performance benchmarks. Several follow-ups agreed (share reports, cost/latency comparison, pilot dataset).

Topics covered:
- Compliance evidence (SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001)
- Authentication and SSO (SAML/Okta)
- RBAC model and session management
- Audit logs, retention, and exportability
- Encryption: at-rest, in-transit, KMS/HSM integration, customer-managed keys
- Deployment options: Hosted, Dedicated (reserved), Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Data retention policies and data deletion
- Pilot scope: performance benchmarks and redacted sample traffic

Action items (short): See action_items field above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Marcus: Hey everyone, thanks for blocking time, really appreciate it. Uh, quick intros from our side, I'm Marcus Lee, AE, and Priya Nair is our SE who will go into architecture.
[00:12] Priya: Hi all, thanks, hi Emma, hi Raj. We'll try to keep this tight, but feel free to interrupt, we want to be sure we capture everything about your compliance needs.
[00:20] Emma: Thanks, Marcus. So to kick off, high level — Silverpike is regulated, payments adjacent, and our security bar is pretty high. Primary asks: SOC two evidence, ISO posture, SSO via Okta, customer-managed keys preferred, and strict audit logging retention.
[00:36] Marcus: Got it. When you say customer-managed keys, are you thinking a cloud KMS integration (AWS KMS / Google CMEK) or on-prem HSMs?
[00:44] Emma: Ideally cloud KMS for now, AWS KMS, but HSM later if we go private / on-prem. The legal team also wants key rotation policies documented.
[00:53] Olivia: Yeah, and to add legal, we need to see the SOC2 Type II report and a DPA draft. Also specifics on data deletion and egress controls — who can pull logs, how long they're retained.
[01:04] Raj: On the technical side, our traffic is mostly short generation calls, peaks ~300 RPS, average 60 QPS outside peak, 8–12 token sequences typically. Pilot intended to test throughput and latency at 99th percentile.
[01:20] Priya: Helpful — that informs batching and model selection. Quick note on SSO: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 with Okta, role mapping for RBAC, and SCIM for provisioning.
[01:30] Leo: Is SCIM available for provisioning groups? We want to sync roles from Okta.
[01:34] Priya: Yes, SCIM for group sync. Role mapping can be done via SAML attributes or SCIM group membership, depending on your identity flow.
[01:41] Emma: We also need per-user audit trails and immutable logs for at least two years. Is that built-in?
[01:46] Marcus: We have audit logs with per-request metadata — token id, model, route, requestor — and export hooks to S3 or your SIEM. Retention defaults can be configured; for Hosted customers we keep logs for X by default, but enterprise plans allow longer retention.
[01:59] Emma: How do you guarantee immutability? We need tamper-evidence, append-only storage or WORM support.
[02:06] Priya: Good question. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with customer S3 buckets with object lock or deliver to your SIEM that supports WORM. For Hosted we offer export snapshots and signed log deliveries; I should follow up with the exact guarantees.
[02:20] Olivia: Also encryption at rest — are keys double-wrapped or tenant isolated? If Redwood holds CMKs, what separation exists?
[02:27] Marcus: Two models: Redwood-managed keys (we manage CMKs) or customer-managed keys via AWS KMS — you control the CMK and Redwood is given decrypt/encrypt permissions only. For Private/on-prem we can support HSM-backed keys.
[02:40] Raj: Latency is critical. If we use customer-managed KMS, any key calls add latency on request path?
[02:46] Priya: We keep the KMS calls out of the hot path for per-token generation. The runtime fetches and caches encryption contexts; unwrap/rotate are async where possible. There may be small overhead on key rotation or initial key fetch.
[02:58] Raj: Ok that helps. For data residency, Silverpike requires EU-only data storage for EU customers. Can we pin region?
[03:05] Marcus: Yes, region pinning is supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be regioned where available; we can route EU workload to EU-only infra and ensure no egress to other regions.
[03:15] Emma: SOC2 question: you mentioned SOC two — do you have Type II and is audit evidence sharable under NDA?
[03:21] Marcus: We do have SOC 2 Type II. We'll share the report under an NDA; I'll send it after the call.
[03:26] Olivia: Please include a summary of control exceptions, if any.
[03:29] Marcus: Will do.
[03:31] Priya: On RBAC, we support granular roles: admin, billing, model-deployer, viewer, and custom roles with scoped permissions. API keys can be tokenized and tied to roles; we also support short-lived session tokens.
[03:44] Leo: Are there per-token cost labels or audit tagging to attribute cost to teams?
[03:49] Marcus: Yes, tagging on requests and usage export is available so you can bill-back.
[03:53] Raj: For the pilot, our success criteria: maintain p99 < 200ms for short responses, and 99.95% availability during the test window.
[04:02] Priya: We'll design the pilot with a canary phase and sustained load tests; we'll propose a config with Dedicated reserved capacity to hit that SLO, or Private if you want isolated infra.
[04:13] Emma: What about breach notification timelines? We need 72-hour notice SLA to our security team.
[04:18] Marcus: Redwood's incident response timeline aligns with typical enterprise agreements; by default we notify customers within 48–72 hours after incident triage for security incidents. We'll include exact SLA language in the DPA.
[04:29] Olivia: On legal terms, we will require subprocessor list, data flow, and an indemnity cap — we'll share a standard questionnaire.
[04:36] Marcus: Perfect. Send that over and we'll respond.
[04:39] Raj: Deep technical — how are model artifacts stored? Are checkpoints encrypted at rest and are there separate tenancy folders?
[04:46] Priya: Model artifacts are encrypted at rest. For Dedicated/Private, the storage can be in your VPC or dedicated bucket. For Hosted, artifacts are tenant-scoped with logical isolation. We'll provide architecture diagrams.
[04:58] Emma: Any certifications planned beyond SOC2/ISO? Like PCI or FedRAMP?
[05:03] Marcus: Not currently pursuing PCI or FedRAMP, but ISO 27001 is in scope; we can discuss specialized compliance for enterprise customers as needed.
[05:12] Leo: For logging, do you provide structured JSON logs per request with user id and request id?
[05:18] Priya: Yes, structured logs with fields: request_id, user_id, model, tokens, route, timestamp. We can stream these to your SIEM in near-real-time.
[05:28] Emma: Data retention and deletion: we need proof of data erasure on termination and a documented process.
[05:34] Marcus: We have documented deletion procedures and can provide a certificate of deletion for resources; for Hosted customers we have standard retention timelines, and for Dedicated/Private we can accommodate custom retention and deletion policies.
[05:45] Raj: Is there support for private networks / VPC peering?
[05:48] Priya: Yes — Private mode gives customer-managed VPC, direct peering, and optional on-prem connectors. Dedicated provides VPC options and private endpoints too.
[05:57] Raj: For encryption key lifecycle, how is rotation handled with zero downtime?
[06:02] Priya: We support key rotation with key versioning and seamless fallback; runtime caches decryption keys to avoid stalls. Rotation is coordinated and can be done with a short overlap window. We'll include recommended rotation cadence.
[06:16] Emma: Any privacy mode for model training — e.g., disable upstream model telemetry so our prompts don't feed future model training?
[06:24] Marcus: We offer telemetry opt-outs at enterprise level. Hosted default does not use customer data for training; we have an explicit setting and contractual language to prevent model training on customer data.
[06:35] Olivia: Can we get logs for admin activity and a history of role changes?
[06:39] Priya: Yes, audit trails include admin activity and role modification events with before/after snapshots.
[06:46] Leo: Do you support MFA enforced for console users?
[06:49] Marcus: Yes, SAML/Okta enforced MFA is supported; console and API token flows can require higher assurance levels.
[06:57] Raj: Are there export controls or restrictions on models/embeddings? We have some regulated PII redaction needs.
[07:05] Priya: We have redaction patterns and suggestions; for PII we recommend pre-filtering and we can help design an inline redact pipeline. Also embedding storage can be encrypted and access limited.
[07:18] Emma: For discovery, what would you need from us to size a Dedicated cluster for the pilot?
[07:22] Priya: Sample traffic profile (QPS distribution), sample prompt sizes, 90/95/99 latency targets, and an estimate of concurrency. Also your choice of model family — open or closed — which affects memory and GPU requirements.
[07:35] Raj: We'll share a csv of traffic and a redacted prompt set.
[07:39] Marcus: Great. Last part — procurement and timeline. What is Silverpike's timeframe?
[07:44] Emma: We're aiming for a Q3 pilot, procurement complete in August, production target Q4 pending pilot results. Security sign-off is gating.
[07:52] Marcus: Understood. We'll aim to get SOC2 and architecture docs to you this week and priya will follow up with a Dedicated/Private config by early next week.
[07:59] Olivia: Quick question on data deletion: do you provide automated scrub for logs or is it manual?
[08:04] Priya: Automated retention policies are configurable and deletions are automated; we can also run on-demand scrubs and provide certificates.
[08:11] Raj: Any limitations on KMS in private mode vs hosted?
[08:15] Priya: In Private mode you can bring your own HSM and keys entirely off our managed plane; Hosted requires integration via cloud KMS APIs.
[08:23] Emma: If we decide hosted for speed of ramp, can we later migrate to Dedicated with retention of keying and logs?
[08:29] Marcus: Yes, we support migration paths; logs and artifacts can be exported and re-ingested into Dedicated/Private setups, though there is an operational cutover. We'll document the migration playbook.
[08:42] Leo: Any known limitations for compliance scanner integrations like CrowdStrike or Splunk?
[08:47] Priya: We have out-of-the-box integrations for common SIEMs via log streaming; for agent-based integrations we can discuss connectors.
[08:56] Emma: Ok, that's helpful. To confirm, deliverables from Redwood: SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, architecture diagram for Dedicated and Private, KMS integration notes, sample retention config, and a pilot proposal.
[09:10] Marcus: Yep, we'll send that.
[09:13] Olivia: We'll review the DPA and return questions.
[09:16] Marcus: Great. Anything else?
[09:18] Raj: No, that's it from my side.
[09:20] Emma: Thanks, looking forward to the docs.
[09:22] Marcus: Appreciate everyone's time. We'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the pricing deep-dive.
[09:27] (call ends — informal wrap)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (SAML as "seml" in automated parts), speaker overlap, and short timestamp granularity is approximate.
